keys.bank_runs_fdic: DOES FDIC INSURANCE PROTECT MY MONEY?
keys.bank_runs_fdic_content_1: FDIC insurance is designed to protect bank depositors in the event that a bank fails. Deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor. Sounds great, right?
keys.bank_runs_fdic_content_2: Not exactly. If a bank fails, where does the FDIC get the money from? They have an insurance fund with 125 billion dollars in it.
keys.bank_runs_fdic_content_3: That sounds like a lot of money until you compare it to the amount of deposits they insure: almost 10 trillion or 10,000 billion dollars.
keys.bank_runs_fdic_content_4: The FDIC even shows on their website that they only have enough money in their insurance fund to cover a little more than 1% of deposits.
keys.bank_runs_fdic_content_5: In the event of a bank failure that exceeded the FDIC insurance fund, it is likely (but not guaranteed) that the US government would print money to make depositors whole.
keys.bank_runs_fdic_content_6: But printing money causes inflation, so it's not a great solution.
keys.bank_runs_how_content_1: Our banking system is 'fractional reserve' which means the banks don't just keep your money in a vault and wait for you to spend it or withdraw it.
keys.bank_runs_how_content_2: Instead, your bank takes your money and lends it out or invests it. This can lock your money up for long periods of time, even though the bank promises you the ability to withdraw your money any time.
keys.bank_runs_how_content_3: So what happens if you try to withdraw your money after the bank has already lent it out or invested it?
keys.bank_runs_how_content_4: It's not a problem if you're the only one trying to withdraw. The bank will just take someone else's money and give it to you instead. But what happens when too many people try to withdraw at the same time?
keys.bank_runs_how_content_5: Lots of people in the USA found out when there was a run on Silicon Valley Bank in March of 2023.
keys.bank_runs_how_content_6: The bank had invested their customers' money in government bonds which were locked for up to 30 years. Even worse, the value of those bonds had fallen dramatically recently, so Silicon Valley Bank couldn't just sell the bonds to get the money of their depositors. They were insolvent. They didn't have enough money to match the withdrawals of their depositors.
keys.bank_runs_how_content_7: As more people found out, the problem only got worse. More withdrawal requests came in, but many weren't processed. Thousands of businesses realized they wouldn't be able to pay their employees due to the bank failing.
keys.bank_runs_how_content_8: The FDIC stepped in and agreed to make depositors whole. Problem solved? Not exactly...
keys.bank_runs_protect: CAN BITCOIN PROTECT ME FROM BANK RUNS?
keys.bank_runs_protect_content_1: Yes, Bitcoin is a full reserve financial system.
keys.bank_runs_protect_content_2: Bank runs are impossible in Bitcoin as long as you withdraw your Bitcoin to your own wallet. Don't leave your bitcoin on an exchange or in a wrapper like a Bitcoin ETF.
keys.bank_runs_protect_content_3: Check out our simple Bitcoin Wallet Guide to learn how to withdraw to your own wallet.
keys.bank_runs_protect_content_4: With Bitcoin, you can finally be in control of your money.
keys.bank_runs_safe: ARE THERE BANKS THAT DON'T USE FRACTIONAL RESERVE?
keys.bank_runs_safe_content_1: Some banks have tried to be 'safe banks' which don't lend out or invest depositor funds.
keys.bank_runs_safe_content_2: Even though these safe banks would have zero risk of bank runs, their applications have been denied by the Federal Reserve. This means they can't legally operate as banks.
keys.bank_runs_safe_content_3: Because they've been blocked from operating, there are no banks today that don't use fractional reserve.
keys.bank_runs_safe_content_4: Fortunately, there is a way to opt out of the fractional reserve system by being your own bank. No, we're not talking about stuffing cash under your mattress.
keys.bank_runs_safe_content_5: Saving in cash is still vulnerable to inflation.
keys.bank_runs_safe_content_6: We're talking about Bitcoin: a new financial system that allows you to be your own bank.
keys.bank_runs_what_content_1: A bank run happens when too many people try to withdraw their money from the bank at the same time.
keys.bank_runs_what_content_2: If banks don't have enough money available to match withdrawals, they can collapse entirely when a bank run happens.

keys.banks_intro_1: Banks have controlled money for centuries, acting as intermediaries for financial transactions and gatekeepers of the monetary system.
keys.banks_intro_2: Bitcoin is a peer-to-peer digital money system that operates without banks or central authorities.
keys.banks_intro_3: But how does the Bitcoin network differ from the traditional banking system? Let's explore the key differences between these two fundamentally different approaches to money.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Bitcoin is permissionless, meaning anyone with internet access can use it without asking for approval from any authority.
keys.point_1_summary_3: - no one can deny you access. Banks, however, can refuse to open accounts, freeze existing accounts, or deny services based on their policies or government regulations.
keys.point_2_summary_1: The Bitcoin network operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year without maintenance windows or holidays. Banks have limited operating hours, close on weekends and holidays, and often have system maintenance periods when services are unavailable.
keys.point_3_summary_1: All Bitcoin transactions are recorded on a public blockchain that anyone can verify and audit.
keys.point_3_summary_2: Banks operate with private ledgers and opaque internal processes that customers cannot independently verify.
keys.point_4_summary_1: With Bitcoin, you can hold your own private keys and have complete control over your money.
keys.point_4_summary_3: to understand self-custody. Banks hold your money in their accounts and can freeze, limit, or restrict access to your funds at any time.
keys.point_5_summary_1: Bitcoin transaction fees are transparent, predictable, and typically very low. Banks often have hidden fees, monthly account fees, overdraft charges, wire transfer fees, ATM fees, and other penalties that can add up significantly over time.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Bitcoin prevents you from spending money you don't have - you can only spend Bitcoin that you actually own. Banks allow overdrafts (spending more than your account balance) and then charge substantial fees for this 'service,' often leading to cascading penalty charges.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Bitcoin transactions are censorship resistant - once broadcast to the network, they cannot be stopped or reversed by any central authority. Banks can block, freeze, reverse, or restrict transactions based on their policies, government orders, or suspicious activity algorithms.

keys.bonds_intro_1: Government bonds are often called 'risk-free' investments and are considered the safest place to store wealth by traditional finance.
keys.bonds_intro_2: Bitcoin is digital money that operates independently of any government or central authority.
keys.bonds_intro_3: But are bonds really risk-free? And how do they compare to Bitcoin as a store of value? Let's examine the key differences between Bitcoin and government bonds.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Bonds are only 'risk-free' in nominal dollar terms, meaning you'll get your dollars back if you hold to maturity. However, this ignores inflation risk, interest rate risk, and the possibility that those dollars will be worth much less when you get them back.
keys.point_1_summary_2: Bitcoin has clear, transparent risks (volatility) but no hidden counterparty risk - you either own your Bitcoin or you don't.
keys.point_2_summary_1: When inflation is higher than bond yields, bondholders lose purchasing power every year. A 2% bond yield with 4% inflation means you're losing 2% of real value annually.
keys.point_2_summary_3: Bitcoin's fixed supply of 21 million coins means it can't be inflated away, but bonds can be devalued by money printing.
keys.point_3_summary_1: During financial crises, bond markets can freeze up and become illiquid. Banks like Silicon Valley Bank got stuck holding bonds that lost significant value when interest rates rose, contributing to their collapse.
keys.point_3_summary_2: Learn how Silicon Valley Bank failed and why Bitcoin is different.
keys.point_3_summary_3: Bitcoin trades 24/7 globally and has never had a liquidity crisis - you can always find a buyer or seller.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Treasury auctions can fail when there aren't enough buyers for government debt. This happened multiple times in recent years, including weak demand for 10-year bonds in 2022 and 30-year bonds in 2023.
keys.point_4_summary_2: Learn more about these failed treasury auctions.
keys.point_4_summary_3: Bitcoin's price is discovered through continuous global markets with no central auction that can fail.
keys.point_5_summary_1: Bond yields are fixed when you buy them. Even if the economy grows rapidly or the currency devalues significantly, your return stays the same.
keys.point_5_summary_2: Bitcoin has the potential for significant appreciation as adoption grows and the fixed supply meets increasing demand.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Most people hold bonds through intermediaries like banks, brokers, or funds, creating counterparty risk. You don't actually own the bonds directly.
keys.point_6_summary_2: With Bitcoin, you can take direct ownership through self-custody, eliminating counterparty risk entirely.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Bonds depend entirely on the government's ability and willingness to pay. If the government faces fiscal crisis, defaults, or decides to inflate away the debt, bondholders suffer.
keys.point_7_summary_2: Bitcoin operates independently of any government and cannot be controlled, inflated, or defaulted on by political authorities.

keys.cash_intro_1: Cash has been used as money for centuries and remains the most common form of physical money worldwide.
keys.cash_intro_2: Bitcoin is digital money created in 2009 that operates independently of any government or central authority.
keys.cash_intro_3: But how does physical cash differ from digital money like Bitcoin? Let's explore the key differences between these two forms of money: Bitcoin & Cash.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Bitcoin can be sent anywhere in the world instantly over the Internet, while cash requires physical presence or trusted intermediaries. You can't email cash, but you can send Bitcoin to anyone with an Internet connection in minutes.
keys.point_2_summary_1: Bitcoin works the same way everywhere in the world - there are no borders in the Bitcoin network. Cash is limited by geography, exchange rates, and local acceptance. Try using US dollars in rural Thailand or Japanese yen in rural Mexico.
keys.point_3_summary_1: Governments can and do invalidate cash overnight through demonetization policies, like India did in 2016 when they banned certain banknotes.
keys.point_3_summary_2: Even without banning certain banknotes, governments constantly devalue cash through inflation.
keys.point_3_summary_3: Bitcoin cannot be invalidated by any government or authority - it exists on a global, decentralized network that no single entity controls.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Cash can be counterfeited, and it's often difficult to detect fake bills without special equipment. Even with security features, counterfeit cash continues to circulate. Bitcoin uses cryptographic proof that makes counterfeiting mathematically impossible.
keys.point_5_summary_1: Cash is issued and controlled by governments, who can print more at will, change designs, or declare certain bills invalid. Bitcoin operates on a decentralized network where no single authority has control over the money supply or rules.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Cash must be stored physically, making it vulnerable to theft, loss, fire, or confiscation. Large amounts require expensive security measures.
keys.point_6_summary_2: But Bitcoin can be securely stored in self-custody
keys.point_6_summary_3: using a smartphone app or specialized wallet, giving you complete control over your money without physical storage risks.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Cash has minimum denominations - you can't split a penny into smaller parts. Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, enabling micropayments and precise transactions of any amount.

keys.cbdc_intro_1: Our world is becoming increasingly digital, and so is our money.
keys.cbdc_intro_2: That begs the question: what do we want our digital money to look like?
keys.cbdc_intro_3: Many countries are exploring issuing a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) which is a fully digital form of our existing government currency.
keys.cbdc_intro_4: Let's take a look at the difference between two forms of digital money: Bitcoin & Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs).
keys.point_10_summary_1: Bitcoin is the most secure computing network that has ever existed and has never been hacked. CBDCs rely on governments and banks to secure the network, which have been hacked countless times throughout history.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Bitcoin is designed to give you total control over your money.
keys.point_1_summary_2: No one can stop you from transacting with Bitcoin.
keys.point_1_summary_3: CBDCs are designed to give governments and central banks total control over your money.
keys.point_1_summary_4: CBDCs limit your privacy and freedom.
keys.point_2_summary_1: Bitcoin never expires and has no monthly fees.
keys.point_2_summary_2: CBDCs can be programmed to expire.
keys.point_2_summary_3: When CBDCs expire, they prevent you from saving for the future.
keys.point_3_summary_1: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million BTC that will ever exist.
keys.point_3_summary_2: CBDCs, much like the government currencies we use today, have no cap on total supply. This lack of cap on total supply allows the government to expand the money supply.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Bitcoin addresses are pseudonymous, which means they are not linked to your real name or identity. CBDCs are directly linked to your real name and identity which enables massive financial surveillance and censorship.
keys.point_5_summary_2: Tens of thousands of independent nodes validate the rules of the network.
keys.point_5_summary_3: CBDCs are centralized in the hands of the government and central banks, which gives them complete control over the CBDC network.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Bitcoin allows anyone to run a node that verifies the rules of the network are being followed. CBDCs don't allow anyone to run nodes and rely on trust in the government and central banks.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Bitcoin is designed to make it impossible for others to freeze your money. CBDCs are designed to make it easy for governments and central banks to freeze your money.
keys.point_8_summary_1: Bitcoin is designed to give you full control over your money.
keys.point_8_summary_2: Just make sure you withdraw it to a self-custody wallet.
keys.point_8_summary_3: When you self-custody your bitcoin, no one can stop you from accessing your money.
keys.point_8_summary_4: CBDCs require you to trust custodians, like a bank or government, to hold your money for you.
keys.point_9_summary_1: Bitcoin has a predictable monetary policy that is fixed in code and can't be changed. CBDCs, like our currencies today, have a monetary policy that can easily be changed.
keys.point_9_summary_2: This results in inflation when politicians print too much money.

keys.crypto_intro_1: The cryptocurrency space has exploded with thousands of different digital tokens and projects.
keys.crypto_intro_2: While Bitcoin was the first and remains the most well-known cryptocurrency, it's fundamentally different from the rest of the crypto industry.
keys.crypto_intro_3: Let's explore the key differences between Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency ecosystem.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Bitcoin's protocol has remained fundamentally unchanged since 2009, providing predictable rules that cannot be easily altered. Most crypto projects frequently update their protocols, change tokenomics, or fork into new versions, creating uncertainty for users.
keys.point_2_summary_1: Bitcoin operates on a truly decentralized network with tens of thousands of independent nodes worldwide. Many crypto projects are controlled by foundations, companies, or small groups of developers who can make unilateral decisions about the protocol's future.
keys.point_3_summary_1: Bitcoin has a hard cap of 21 million coins that will ever exist, making it the scarcest digital asset. Most crypto projects have unlimited supplies, inflationary mechanisms, or can mint new tokens at will, diluting holder value over time.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Bitcoin has one simple purpose: peer-to-peer digital money. Anyone can understand and use it with basic knowledge. Many crypto projects involve complex smart contracts, DeFi protocols, or governance mechanisms that require technical expertise to use safely.
keys.point_5_summary_1: Bitcoin uses Proof of Work consensus, which has been battle-tested for over 15 years without a single successful attack on the main network. Many crypto projects use experimental consensus mechanisms like Proof of Stake or delegated systems that haven't proven their long-term security.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Bitcoin serves as digital money - a store of value and medium of exchange. Most crypto tokens are utility tokens for specific platforms, governance tokens, or speculative assets with unclear real-world value propositions.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Bitcoin becomes stronger under attack and has survived every crisis, ban, and criticism thrown at it. Most crypto projects are fragile and can collapse from regulatory pressure, technical failures, or market downturns.
keys.point_8_summary_1: Bitcoin has no CEO, no company behind it, and no single point of failure. Many crypto projects are backed by venture capital firms, have identifiable leadership teams, or depend on specific companies for their continued operation.

keys.fine_art_intro_1: Fine art has been a luxury investment for centuries and is often seen as a store of value by wealthy collectors.
keys.fine_art_intro_2: Bitcoin is digital money that is also seen by many as a store of value and investment.
keys.fine_art_intro_3: But how does physical artwork differ from digital money like Bitcoin? Let's take a look at the differences between two forms of investment: Bitcoin & Fine Art.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Bitcoin is perfectly fungible, meaning every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable - one bitcoin equals one bitcoin anywhere in the world. Fine art is non-fungible by nature, with each piece being unique in its creation, history, condition, and provenance, making direct comparisons and valuations extremely difficult.
keys.point_2_summary_1: Bitcoin trades on a global 24/7 market where anyone with internet access can buy or sell instantly. Fine art requires specialized auction houses like Sotheby's or Christie's, private dealers, or exclusive galleries. Sales can take months to arrange and complete, with limited market access and irregular trading opportunities.
keys.point_3_summary_1: Buying or selling bitcoin typically costs less than 1% in fees, often much less. Fine art sales involve substantial costs including buyer's premiums (10-25%), seller's commissions (10-15%), insurance, transportation, storage, and authentication fees. These combined costs can easily exceed 30-40% of the artwork's value in a single transaction.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Bitcoin can be divided into 100 million smaller units called satoshis, making it perfect for transactions of any size from microtransactions to large purchases. Fine art cannot be divided - you cannot own a fraction of a painting or sell just part of a sculpture. This indivisibility limits investment flexibility and liquidity options.
keys.point_5_summary_1: Bitcoin ownership and authenticity can be cryptographically verified on the blockchain by anyone with basic technical knowledge. Fine art requires expensive expert authentication, provenance research, and scientific analysis. Even with expert verification, forgeries regularly fool the art world, and authentication disputes can destroy an artwork's value overnight. Bitcoin, on the other hand, cannot be forged or counterfeited.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Bitcoin, when backed up properly, cannot be destroyed by floods, fires, earthquakes, hurricanes, theft, or other disasters. Fine art is vulnerable to all forms of physical destruction and deterioration. Even with expensive climate-controlled storage and comprehensive insurance, artworks can be damaged by environmental factors, accidents, or natural disasters, potentially losing all value.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Bitcoin can be bought and sold by anyone with internet access and a small amount of money to invest. Fine art investment is largely limited to wealthy collectors due to high minimum prices, exclusive auction access, storage requirements, insurance costs, and the specialized knowledge needed to navigate the art market successfully.

keys.gold_intro_1: Gold has been used as money for thousands of years and is seen by many as a financial safe haven.
keys.gold_intro_2: Bitcoin is digital money created in 2009 and is also seen by many as a financial safe haven.
keys.gold_intro_3: But how does a physical metal like gold differ from a digital money like Bitcoin? Let's take a look at the differences between two forms of money: Bitcoin & Gold.
keys.point_1_summary_1: Because Bitcoin is digital, it can be sent almost instantly for very low fees by anyone with an Internet connection. Because Gold is physical, it cannot be moved across the Internet and must be physically shipped to transfer ownership.
keys.point_2_summary_1: Bitcoin is a digitally native asset, which means you can transfer full ownership of it over the Internet. Some companies offer the ability to buy gold online without receiving the actual physical gold, instead trusting the company to hold the gold for you. This is more like a Digital IOU since you only own a promise from the company instead of the actual asset.

keys.point_3_summary_2: New gold supply is pulled out of the ground each year, resulting in inflation of the total supply. It's estimated that the total supply of gold increases by about 1.6% per year, which means your slice of the pie shrinks by 1.6% per year.
keys.point_3_summary_3: This is less than fiat inflation, but still inflation.
keys.point_3_summary_4: With Bitcoin, your slice of the pie never shrinks.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Gold has an elastic supply, meaning that as the price of gold rises, there is a greater incentive to mine more gold. This often puts downward pressure on the gold price as new mines come online.
keys.point_4_summary_2: With Bitcoin, no matter how high the price goes, you can't make more than 21M Bitcoin.
keys.point_4_summary_3: Bitcoin is the first asset with an inelastic relationship between price and supply.
keys.point_5_summary_2: Tens of thousands of independent nodes validate the rules of the network.
keys.point_5_summary_3: Users can take self-custody of their Bitcoin by downloading an app.
keys.point_5_summary_4: While it is possible to self-custody physical gold, most physical gold is stored in huge vaults owned by custodians which makes it physically centralized.
keys.point_6_summary_1: With Bitcoin, it's incredibly easy to verify that you have real Bitcoin by taking self-custody of your coins and running a full node.
keys.point_6_summary_2: Self-custody is as simple as downloading an app.
keys.point_6_summary_3: A full node is a simple piece of software that ensures the rules of the network are being followed, and verifies that you have real Bitcoin.
keys.point_6_summary_4: Physical gold can be very difficult to verify as authentic. Even if you verify the outer section of physical gold is real, the inside of your physical gold piece could be Tungsten or another metal that is not gold. The only way to truly verify you own the physical gold you think you do is to melt it down.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Just like there are 100 cents in 1 dollar, there are 100,000,000 sats in 1 Bitcoin. This enables Bitcoin to be used for all scales of purchases, including microtransactions as small as a few cents.
keys.point_7_summary_2: This makes Bitcoin good for business.
keys.point_7_summary_3: Because physical gold is hard to divide, it can't be easily used for purchases, especially small purchases.

keys.point_7_summary_1: Every bitcoin is identical and interchangeable - one bitcoin equals one bitcoin anywhere in the world. Every piece of real estate is unique with different locations, conditions, and characteristics, making it difficult to price and compare properties.

keys.point_3_summary_1: Bitcoin operates on a transparent blockchain where all transactions can be verified by anyone. Credit card networks operate as closed, proprietary systems where transaction details are hidden from public view.
keys.point_3_summary_2: This transparency makes Bitcoin more trustworthy and allows for independent verification of the network's integrity.
keys.point_4_summary_1: Credit card companies can freeze accounts, block transactions, or deny service at any time. Bitcoin cannot be frozen or controlled by any central authority.
keys.point_4_summary_2: With Bitcoin, you maintain control over your money and cannot be cut off from the payment system.
keys.point_5_summary_1: Credit cards create debt that can accumulate high interest rates if not paid off quickly, sometimes exceeding 25% annually.
keys.point_5_summary_2: Bitcoin transactions are final settlements with no debt creation - you can only spend Bitcoin you actually own.
keys.point_6_summary_1: Bitcoin allows for self-custody, meaning you can hold and control your own money without relying on banks or payment processors.
keys.point_6_summary_3: to understand how you can take control of your own money. Credit cards always require intermediaries like banks and payment processors.
keys.point_7_summary_1: Bitcoin works 24/7 globally with no business hours or geographic restrictions.
keys.point_7_summary_2: Credit card networks have business hours, maintenance windows, and geographic limitations that can prevent transactions from processing.
keys.visa_intro_1: Credit cards and Bitcoin are both payment systems, but they work very differently.
keys.visa_intro_2: Credit cards like Visa are closed networks controlled by financial institutions, while Bitcoin is an open network that anyone can use.
keys.visa_intro_3: Let's take a look at the differences between these two payment rails: Bitcoin & Visa.

keys.accounting_description: Learn how to properly account for Bitcoin payments in your business accounting.
keys.accounting_s1_c1: Accepting Bitcoin has many benefits like accepting payments with lower fees & getting more customers.
keys.accounting_s1_c2: If you use a Hybrid Wallet from our Wallet Guide and automatically sell 100% of the Bitcoin you receive for dollars, you don't need to make any changes to your current accounting.
keys.accounting_s1_c4: However, if you keep some of the Bitcoin payments you receive as Bitcoin, you'll need to keep track of a few details for your accounting. This can seem intimidating at first, but is actually quite simple.
keys.accounting_s1_c5: Please note: this guide is for informational purposes only and is not to be considered tax advice.
keys.accounting_s1_c6: If you need tax advice, we highly recommend Satoshi Pacioli Accounting Services, an accounting firm that specializes in Bitcoin accounting.
keys.accounting_s2_c1: Tracking your cost basis is going to be the biggest difference between accounting for dollars and accounting for Bitcoin. Even if you view your business entirely in terms of Bitcoin, you need to report the dollar value of each transaction on your taxes.
keys.accounting_s2_c2: If you use QuickBooks, you can do this automatically using the Bitcoin Sync plugin.
keys.accounting_s2_c3: If you don't use QuickBooks, we recommend Satoshi Pacioli Accounting Services, an accounting firm that specializes in Bitcoin accounting.
keys.accounting_s2_c4: To do this manually, you simply need to keep track of the amount of Bitcoin you received and the dollar value of the Bitcoin transaction on that day.
keys.accounting_s2_c5: You can view the current dollar price of Bitcoin here.
keys.accounting_s2_c6: Keep track of this information in an Excel spreadsheet and give it to your accountant.
keys.accounting_s2_c7: You can also import this data into Excel automatically.
keys.accounting_s2_c8: You can also view the historical dollar price of Bitcoin on days in the past, so you don't have to do this every day.
keys.accounting_s3_c1: If you use a Hybrid Wallet from our Wallet Guide and automatically sell 100% of the Bitcoin you receive for dollars, you don't need to make any changes to your current accounting.
keys.accounting_s3_c3: If you choose to spend or sell some of the Bitcoin you receive after holding it for a while, you simply need to add the price you sold it for into your Excel spreadsheet that tracks your cost basis.
keys.accounting_s3_c4: For example, if you received $100 worth of Bitcoin on January 1st and decided to sell or spend it on February 1st at a new value of $110, you would need to record a $10 capital gain in your accounting.
keys.accounting_s3_c5: This can also work the opposite way. For example, if you received $100 worth of Bitcoin on January 1st and decided to sell or spend it on February 1st at a new value of $90, you would need to record a $10 capital loss in your accounting.

keys.common_bitcoin_afford: I CAN'T AFFORD A WHOLE BITCOIN
keys.common_bitcoin_afford_content_1: A dollar is made up of 100 cents. A bitcoin is made up of 100,000,000 (100 million) sats.
keys.common_bitcoin_afford_content_2: You don’t have to own a whole bitcoin. Most people just own sats. Sats are fractions of a bitcoin. For example, if 1 whole bitcoin is $100,000 then $1 buys you 1,000 sats!
keys.common_bitcoin_energy_content_1: Bitcoin uses energy to secure the network and protect your money.
keys.common_bitcoin_energy_content_2: Bitcoin uses a significant amount of energy, and this is a great thing for many reasons.
keys.common_bitcoin_energy_list_2: Bitcoin helps stabilize energy grids with bitcoin mining.
keys.common_bitcoin_energy_list_3: Bitcoin reduces emissions from oil drilling.
keys.common_bitcoin_energy_list_4: Bitcoin uses less energy than Americans use for Christmas Lights each year.
keys.common_bitcoin_energy_list_5: Bitcoin is the greenest industry on Earth!
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_1: You may have heard about a 'Bitcoin hack' online or on the news. Most people read these articles and believe the Bitcoin network has been hacked. However, the Bitcoin network has never been hacked.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_10: The government can't print more bitcoin and cause inflation.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_11: Bitcoin in self-custody is your money, thanks to the power of the Bitcoin network.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_2: What's the Bitcoin network? Well, think of the Bitcoin network as train tracks. The trains riding on the train tracks of the Bitcoin network are Bitcoin transactions.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_3: When you read about a Bitcoin hack in the news, you're reading about a custodian (like FTX) getting hacked or going bankrupt.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_4: Custodians are companies that hold your bitcoin for you. However, that comes with a risk: losing your bitcoin when the company mismanages it, steals it, or goes out of business.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_5: This happened most recently with FTX.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_6: Everyone who trusted FTX with their bitcoin lost their bitcoin. Everyone who held their bitcoin in self-custody was completely unaffected by FTX. That is the power of bitcoin in self-custody: true control of your money.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_7: Instead of leaving your bitcoin on an exchange or in a wrapper like an ETF, hold it in your own wallet for all the freedom benefits.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_8: When you self-custody your bitcoin, your money is protected by the Bitcoin network. It's the most secure financial network in the world.
keys.common_bitcoin_hacked_content_9: In self-custody, Sam from FTX can't steal your bitcoin from you.
keys.common_bitcoin_volatile: I HEARD BITCOIN IS VOLATILE. IS THAT SAFE?
keys.common_bitcoin_volatile_content_1: In the short term, the exchange rate of Bitcoin tends to fluctuate. This is called volatility.
keys.common_bitcoin_volatile_content_2: But the volatility you see on a day-to-day basis 'disappears' in the long term.
keys.common_bitcoin_volatile_content_3: Bitcoin continues to get less and less volatile over time. As more people use Bitcoin as a long term savings account, the more its value stabilizes.
keys.common_bitcoin_volatile_content_4: Many people choose to store value in Bitcoin for many years as a safe way to minimize the risk of volatility and protect their purchasing power over time.
keys.common_bitcoin_volatile_content_5: In some countries, such as Venezuela, Sudan, Lebanon, Syria, Argentina, Turkey, Brazil, and so many others, the value of the local currency inflates away so quickly that Bitcoin is seen as the more stable way to save money.

keys.inflation_issuance_c1: Inflation is essentially your piece of the 'money pie' getting smaller each year. So does Bitcoin have inflation?
keys.inflation_issuance_c2: Bitcoin has a fixed supply of 21,000,000 (21 million) bitcoin that will ever exist. The 21 million supply limit is fixed in code and secured by the most powerful computing network in the world, called The Bitcoin Network. This limit cannot be changed.
keys.inflation_issuance_c3: While Bitcoin doesn't have inflation, it does have issuance. Issuance is the percent of new Bitcoin mined each year. Bitcoin miners secure the network, process Bitcoin transactions, and get paid for their work. Bitcoin miners get paid with this new issuance (until it runs out) and also get paid transaction fees.
keys.inflation_issuance_c4: More than 95% of all bitcoin have already been mined. More than 99% of all 21 million bitcoin will have been mined by the year 2035, and the remaining less than 1% will be mined by the year 2140.
keys.inflation_issuance_c5: Even though there is still some issuance left until the fixed supply of 21 million bitcoin, the entire point is that your slice of the 21 million bitcoin pie never gets smaller. This is in sharp contrast to the government currencies we use. In those systems, your slice of the pie gets smaller every year when more money is printed from thin air.

keys.lightning_description: Lightning wallets enable you to send Bitcoin quickly and cheaply while still maintaining your personal sovereignty.
keys.lightning_question_1: WHAT TRADE-OFF BALANCE IS RIGHT FOR ME?
keys.lightning_s1_c1: Lightning enables you to send Bitcoin payments quickly and cheaply.
keys.lightning_s1_c2: It's important to know that using lightning comes with trade-offs. In exchange for faster, cheaper Bitcoin payments, you often sacrifice some security.
keys.lightning_s1_c3: In general, Lightning should only be used with small amounts of bitcoin. You should only ever store large amounts of bitcoin in a hardware wallet.
keys.lightning_s1_c4: Check out our Hardware Wallet Guide for more info.
keys.lightning_s1_c5: Not all Lightning wallets are the same. You can determine which wallet has the right set of trade-offs for you by asking one simple question:
keys.lightning_s2_c1: One of the innovations of Bitcoin is the ability to store it without relying on a custodian, like a bank. Self-custody wallets unlock the full power of Bitcoin.
keys.lightning_s2_c2: With a self-custody wallet, you are the only one with the ability to spend or transfer your money. No one can stop you, censor you, or steal from you when you use a self-custody wallet. These are also called non-custodial wallets.
keys.lightning_s2_c3: The most sovereign way to use Lightning is by running your own node.
keys.lightning_s2_c4: This guide is focused on simple Lightning wallets that don't require your own node.
keys.lightning_s2_c5: It's important to know that even using a non-custodial Lightning wallet, you are still trusting the wallet creator not to push a malicious app update and steal your funds.
keys.lightning_s3_c1: Custodial wallets are wallets where you are not in control of your money.
keys.lightning_s3_c2: These wallets are more similar to the banking system where you must trust a third party to give you access to your money. If your Bitcoin is on an exchange, you are using a custodial wallet.
keys.lightning_s3_c3: Custodial wallets can seem convenient, but the custodian has the technical ability to steal all user funds at any time.
keys.lightning_s3_c4: Some people prefer custodial Lightning wallets for small amounts of bitcoin because of their ease of use. Just remember: not your keys, not your coins!
keys.lightning_s4_c1: With all of this in mind, you can now choose the lightning wallet that has the right trade-off balance for you.

keys.wallets_s3_c1: Custodial wallets are wallets where you are not in control of your money.
keys.wallets_s3_c2: These wallets are more similar to the banking system where you must trust a third party to give you access to your money. If your Bitcoin is on an exchange, you are using a custodial wallet.
keys.wallets_s3_c3: If you bought a Bitcoin ETF, you are using a custodial wallet that doesn't allow you to withdraw to self-custody.
keys.wallets_s3_c4: Custodial wallets can seem convenient, but the custodian has the technical ability to steal all user funds at any time.
keys.wallets_s3_c5: Not your keys, not your coins!
keys.wallets_s4_c1: Cold wallets store the keys to your Bitcoin in a manner that never exposes them to the internet.
keys.wallets_s4_c2: This significantly limits the attack vectors that a thief might use to try to steal your Bitcoin, and is best used for large sums of Bitcoin that you don't need to transfer often.
keys.wallets_s4_c3: You can think of a cold wallet as a long term savings account, also known as cold storage.
keys.wallets_s5_c1: Hot wallets store the keys to your Bitcoin on a device that is connected to the internet, like your phone.
keys.wallets_s5_c2: Hot wallets are generally considered safe, but they could have more security vulnerabilities than cold wallets.
keys.wallets_s5_c3: You can think of a hot wallet like you would a physical wallet. You wouldn't store your entire savings in your wallet, but you would store some spending money.
keys.wallets_s5_c4: Hot wallets make it much easier to spend your Bitcoin without having to pull your entire savings out of cold storage.
keys.wallets_s6_c1: When you set up your Bitcoin wallet, your device will generate a recovery phrase. This recovery phrase (also called a seed phrase) contains 12 or 24 words.
keys.wallets_s6_c2: If you ever lose access to your wallet or your device stops working, you can input this recovery phrase into a new wallet to regain access to your Bitcoin.
keys.wallets_s6_c3: Most wallets include a sheet of paper to write down your recovery phrase, but lots of people prefer to back up this phrase on steel instead. This makes it much less likely to lose your recovery phrase in the event of a natural disaster like a fire or a flood.
keys.wallets_s6_c4: Jameson Lopp has tested 70 steel backup kits to help you pick the one that is right for you.
